ModuleName: Final HCI Evaluation, Reflection, and Lessons Learned
CourseName: CEN3722 - Introduction to Human Computer Interfaces

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: A structured outline of the module's core topics covering HCI theory application, review of analysis and prototyping phases, evaluation methods, and lessons learned, used by instructors to organize content delivery and by learners to navigate what will be covered.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: This HTML page lists the key topics covered in the Final HCI Evaluation, Reflection, and Lessons Learned module—including how HCI theory shaped design decisions and how foundational concepts connect to final product outcomes—serving as a navigational overview for learners and instructors to understand the module's scope before engaging with its materials.

Artifacts.Name: Connecting HCI Theory to Design Outcomes
Artifacts.Description: Explains how HCI theories (such as mental models, affordances, and feedback principles) directly influence concrete design decisions, helping learners connect academic concepts to real interface outcomes.

Artifacts.Name: Review of the Analysis Phase
Artifacts.Description: Reviews the user analysis phase of the HCI design process—covering user research, needs identification, and task analysis—to help learners understand why thorough upfront analysis drives all later design decisions.

Artifacts.Name: Review of the Prototyping Phase
Artifacts.Description: Reviews the prototyping phase of user-centered design, covering types of prototypes, their purpose as testable and disposable representations, and how they enable early assumption-testing and iterative course correction.

Artifacts.Name: Review of the Evaluation Phase
Artifacts.Description: Reviews the evaluation phase of user-centered design, covering usability testing methods, expert review techniques, and how evaluation reveals gaps between designer intent and actual user experience.

Artifacts.Name: Structured Feedback on Design Quality
Artifacts.Description: Covers how to give, receive, and act on structured design feedback from peers, stakeholders, and usability experts, helping learners interpret critique and use it to improve interface quality.

Artifacts.Name: Process Execution and Team Collaboration
Artifacts.Description: Addresses the practical execution of HCI design projects, covering team roles, communication, planning, and documentation practices that determine whether a project succeeds beyond individual technical skill.

Artifacts.Name: Reflection and Lessons Learned
Artifacts.Description: Guides learners through post-project reflection in HCI, explaining how to identify what worked, what failed, and what lessons can be carried forward to improve future design practice.
